_doc: Remote NVMe A/B for cardinality-cliff #1: checkpoint durability via one syncfs() barrier (--wal-checkpoint-syncfs on) vs the per-stream fdatasync loop (baseline), on Titanium NVMe (c4d-standard-16-lssd, 8 vCPU). This is the environment where the optimization's premise holds: per-file fdatasync is an expensive ~1ms hardware barrier, so the checkpoint's O(N_touched) storm (measured ~1.4s/shard at 200k) steals device budget from commits. syncfs collapses that to ONE barrier. Tests at 200k AND 500k streams (the storm is worst at 500k). Same shards(4)/cpu(8)/conns(256) as the wal-shard-sweep baseline so numbers are comparable. If syncfs raises throughput here, merge the flag.
